article.title: Artículo cero con transporte mediante by
article.part: Artículos, determinantes y cuantificación — Articles, determiners, and quantification

claims.summary: English conventionally uses by plus a transport noun without an article to express means of transport, as in by car, by bus or by train.
When referring to a particular vehicle, English commonly uses in or on with a determiner; the conventional pedestrian expression is on foot rather than by foot.

article.title: Adjetivos participiales en -ing/-ed
article.part: Adjetivos, comparación y adverbios — Adjectives, comparison, and adverbs

claims.summary: With many adjective pairs in -ing and -ed, the -ing form describes the effect or quality that produces a reaction, while the -ed form describes the experienced reaction or state.
The contrast between -ing and -ed adjectives is not simply a person-versus-thing distinction; the relevant distinction concerns causing versus experiencing the state or reaction.

claims.summary: The modal verb can is used to express present or general ability.
Can is followed by the base form of the main verb without to, is invariant across persons, forms negatives with cannot/can’t, and forms questions by placing can before the subject.
